briefing.headline: OpenAI and xAI accelerate frontier model releases as US tightens export controls on advanced chips

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race intensifies with multiple frontier model launches this month. Geopolitical tensions rise over compute access while safety concerns mount around agentic systems. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI ships o4-preview with native multi-agent orchestration. Anthropic counters with Claude 4 Opus featuring enhanced reasoning. Google DeepMind debuts Gemini 3, Meta open-sources Llama 4, while xAI's Grok-3 targets real-time knowledge integration.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: New NIST guidelines emphasize runtime monitoring for agent swarms. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level, with early pilots in automotive CAN bus and BCI showing 98% attack mitigation.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC ramps 2nm production for AI accelerators. Microsoft announces $40B hyperscale expansion in Texas and UAE. NVIDIA Blackwell clusters reach 100k GPU deployments at major labs.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent coordination protocols become the decisive factor in achieving reliable superintelligence by 2028?
